audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating cash as entirely excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $4,288.124 million, or $13.29 per share; 13.7% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash and short-term investments directly to equity value even though an operating-liquidity reserve would not be distributable.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary ongoing cash requirements are for merchandise inventory purchases, payroll, operating and variable lease costs, taxes, capital expenditures related to our new and existing stores, and investments in distribution centers, information systems, and buying and corporate offices.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the entire balance is demonstrated, but the amount actually required for operations is unresolved. The maximum exposure is large enough to materially alter intrinsic value and the buy-below threshold, although removing all cash would reduce base value from $96.94 to about $83.65 per share and would not reverse the conclusion that the $231.255 market price exceeds estimated value.
audit_findings.action: Determine unrestricted cash available after minimum liquidity, seasonal working capital, the filed $1.1 billion fiscal-2026 capital-expenditure plan, purchase commitments, and near-term obligations; rerun the bridge and all per-share values using only defensible excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may not be charged for the reinvestment that produces it
audit_findings.magnitude: computed initial reinvestment of approximately $89.2 million at 3% growth and $178.4 million at 6% growth using 64.6% RONTA; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Required incremental investment would reduce forecast owner earnings and terminal cash flow before discounting; omission would particularly affect the base and bull scenarios.
audit_findings.evidence: Capital expenditures for fiscal 2026 are projected to be approximately $1.1 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation shows growth applied to the anchor but does not establish whether owner earnings already deduct all growth capital or only maintenance capital. The filed $1.1 billion fiscal-2026 capital-expenditure plan combines maintenance and growth uses, so it cannot resolve the omission or its materiality. The RONTA-based initial charges demonstrate plausible value leakage, but a complete scenario rerun is needed.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile historical owner earnings to total capital expenditures, identify maintenance versus growth investment, then deduct scenario-specific reinvestment implied by 64.6% RONTA throughout the explicit forecast, fade period, and terminal year and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring property-sale gain may remain in the trend history
audit_findings.magnitude: $61.6 million pretax; approximately $46.7 million after tax at the filed 24.2% fiscal-2024 rate; computed sensitivity approximately $14 million of anchor OE and $0.62 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in the fiscal-2024 observation, the nonrecurring gain raises historical owner earnings and therefore the fitted log-trend anchor and all forecast cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: In fiscal 2024, the Company completed the sale of a packaway warehouse facility and recognized a pre-tax gain on sale of $ 61.6 million which was included within Selling, general and administrative on the Consolidated Statements of Earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the gain was removed is unresolved, but its scale is not material to the valuation conclusion. A removal using the filed tax rate and the supplied ten-year log trend reduces the anchor by approximately 0.7% and base value by roughly $0.62 per share, versus the $96.94 base value, the $27.87 bear-to-bull range, and the $134.32 gap between base value and market price.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the fiscal-2024 owner-earnings reconciliation for an after-tax removal of the $61.6 million gain; if absent, remove it and refit the trend to confirm the computed sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: The trend may mix 52-week and 53-week fiscal years
audit_findings.magnitude: computed pro-rata extra-week amount approximately $36.6 million; approximately $8.6 million of anchor OE and $0.38 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: An unnormalized extra week would inflate the fiscal-2023 owner-earnings observation and modestly raise the fitted log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that fiscal 2023 had 53 weeks, but the record does not establish whether normalization occurred. A mechanical 52/53 normalization of the corresponding $1,938.2 million observation produces only about a 0.45% anchor reduction and a $0.38-per-share base-value reduction, approximately 0.4% of the $96.94 base value and far below the $27.87 scenario range.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the fiscal-2023 trend input and any 52-week normalization; if none was made, rerun using company-reported extra-week results if available, with the 52/53 pro-rata sensitivity as a reasonableness check.
